gen-dafont-azonix-gf-miriam-libre: Miriam Libre reads sturdy and friendly, its lowercase standing tall with the weight of drawn wire and an s that opens up. Azonix above it is the real draw: wide, crisp and commanding.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-mochiy-pop-one: Azonix has capitals barely taller than its lowercase, so words take a beat to knit back together as you read. It handles the headline, while Mochiy Pop One does the talking with its huge lowercase eyes.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Azonix takes the top with a commanding, wide-mouthed stance. Mochiy Pop P One follows in a plain sans, its big lowercase spread out with generous space between every letter, so the two feel like a shout and an easy answer.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-montserrat-underlin: Montserrat Underline reads open and breathing, with oversized lowercase beside its capitals. Azonix sits against it as the firmer voice, wide and authoritative, making the pairing feel like a command followed by a conversation.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-mozilla-headline: Mozilla Headline reads big-bodied and friendly, with a splayed c terminal that gives its sans-serif lowercase some character. Mozilla Headline would carry a long passage comfortably, while Azonix keeps the flat, fineliner-like line up top.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-mozilla-text: Mozilla Text reads bold for a body face, since its lowercase stands so tall, with terminals that flare outward. And over a long passage Azonix stays the crisp, bent-pipe-cleaner voice above while the text keeps its sturdy rhythm.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-nata-sans: Capitals barely rising above the lowercase give Azonix a wide, crisp, commanding look that stays sharp even when shrunk. Nata Sans does the quiet work below, a plain sans with open curves and a technical-pen steadiness.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-nobile: Commanding Azonix is wide and crisp, with crossbars matching its stems in thickness. Nobile, a sans with minimal gap between x-height and caps and open mouths, would read smoothly over a long passage.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-nokora: Nokora reads clean and friendly, its wide-open s never tightening and its lowercase laying a dark stripe through each line. And over a long passage that sturdiness holds up, while Azonix bends its straw-like lines above.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Noto Kufi Arabic brings a welcoming gap in its c and a modern look. Azonix, with no thick-thin swing at all, sits above it in a wide, crisp, commanding line, and the two feel built from the same flat, unfussy stuff.
